title: Structure Over Scale: Rethinking Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
abstract: arXiv:2611.27148v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is often framed as a choice between the expressivity of Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) and the efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). We find that this framing misses an important variable: the geometry of the update. Under a common cold-start GRPO protocol, LoRA exhibits rank collapse: performance remains broadly stable at low rank, then fails abruptly as rank increases. On DeepMath-Hard, for example, accuracy drops from 73.1% at r=64 to 4.7% at r=128. In contrast, Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) and Quantum-Informed Tensor Adaptation (QuanTA) remain stable over a wider tested optimization region and are competitive with FFT while updating less than 0.6% of the model parameters. Spectral analysis reveals a corresponding difference in learned update structure: collapsed LoRA concentrates its update energy into relatively few effective directions, whereas structured adapters

translated_title: 结构重于规模：重新思考可验证奖励强化学习中的适配方法
translated_abstract: 可验证奖励强化学习通常被框架化为在全参数微调的表达能力与低秩适配的高效率之间做选择。我们发现这一框架忽略了一个重要变量：更新的几何结构。在常见的冷启动GRPO协议下，LoRA表现出“秩坍缩”现象：性能在低秩时大致保持稳定，但随着秩的增大却会突然失效。例如在DeepMath-Hard数据集上，准确率从r=64时的73.1%骤降至r=128时的4.7%。相比之下，权重分解低秩适配和量子启发张量适配在更广的测试优化区域内保持稳定，并且在仅更新不到0.6%模型参数的情况下与全参数微调表现相当。谱分析揭示了所学更新结构的相应差异：发生坍缩的LoRA将更新能量集中在相对较少的有效方向上，而结构化适配器……
tldr: 该研究发现在可验证奖励强化学习训练中，LoRA会随秩增大出现性能骤降的“秩坍缩”现象，而DoRA和QuanTA等结构化适配方法凭借更优的更新几何结构，仅更新不到0.6%的参数即可达到与全参数微调相当的效果，表明更新的结构比规模更关键。
en_tdlr: Under RLVR training, LoRA abruptly fails as rank increases due to "rank collapse," while structured adapters like DoRA and QuanTA remain stable and match full fine-tuning while updating less than 0.6% of parameters, showing that update geometry matters more than scale.
